messages:
jen: Heads-up: hitting SSL cert verify errors on Windows venv with async Python SDK (3.8). Sync client OK.

sahil: Can you paste traceback + python/openSSL info?

jen: Traceback: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1007)
python: CPython 3.8.16 64-bit, OpenSSL 1.1.1k (company distro). Minimal repro uses asyncio + AsyncClient.

tkim: Thanks. This smells like env/CA bundle handling differences between requests (sync) and aiohttp (async) on Windows. Sync honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/certifi; async sometimes doesn't.

sahil: Did you try SSL_CERT_FILE? Windows python often only respects that.

jen: Tried both env vars, no luck. Workaround: creating ssl.SSLContext(cafile=path) and injecting into client internals fixed it.

tkim: Action: add AsyncClient.__init__(ca_file: Optional[str]=None) with fallback explicit -> SSL_CERT_FILE -> certifi.where(), and make async retry/backoff match sync. Also fix typing stubs so mypy on 3.8 won't fail.

sahil: Add a windows-only integration test (skip unless sys.platform=='win32') and run windows-latest in CI for 3.8, 3.11, 3.12. Also update quickstart to show os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE']=certifi.where() as a temporary workaround.

jen: Good plan. Please call out in docs that enterprise installers that provide custom CA bundles should set ca_file or SSL_CERT_FILE explicitly.

tkim: Will open PR and GH issue with repro & logs.

devex-bot: PR opened by tkim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/472
